messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-03-18T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up

Hi Emma,

Thanks again for the call today — great to learn more about FintechCo's verification pipeline. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so Rafael (copied) and I can size a Dedicated capacity recommendation: 

Recap:
- Primary use: real-time document understanding + conversational verification for customer onboarding.
- SLA targets: p95 latency target ~500ms for short flows, acceptable p95 up to 1s for longer verification steps.
- Data residency: US-only; interested in Dedicated in a VPC (not hosted public API).

Sizing inputs we need from you (quick asks):
1) Target TPS (average & peak) and expected concurrency (simultaneous requests). Example: average 50 TPS, peak 300 TPS, concurrency 120.
2) Token mix: average prompt tokens and average completion tokens; percent distribution of short vs long queries.
3) Typical model(s) you expect to run (open models or custom-fine-tuned) and any quantization constraints.
4) Preferred GPU family (H100 vs A100) or flexibility on instance types.

I attached our dedicated sizing template to fill — if you can drop a quick traffic sample or a week of request counts, that will help Rafael size more accurately. Next steps: Rafael to produce a preliminary cluster recommendation once we have the inputs; we can then schedule a technical deep-dive to validate latency/concurrency assumptions.

Would you be able to share the TPS/concurrency and token distribution by EOD tomorrow? If not, earliest time that works.

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: redwood_dedicated_sizing_template.xlsx
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-19T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up

Hi Marissa,

Thanks — attaching a filled version of your template (fintechco_capacity_input_v1.xlsx) and a short traffic export for last 7 days. Answers below inline: 

1) TPS / concurrency:
- Typical sustained TPS (queries/sec): ~120 TPS
- Peak TPS (short bursts, up to 10m windows): ~450 TPS
- Concurrent requests we see during peaks: ~200 concurrent calls

2) Token mix:
- Average prompt tokens: 65 tokens
- Average completion tokens: 180 tokens
- Distribution: ~55% short (<80 tokens total), ~35% medium (80-300 tokens), ~10% long (>300 tokens).

3) Models:
- Running a trimmed/flan-open model (fine-tuned internally). We expect to move to a 70B open variant; currently using a 34B. Quantization okay but prefer 8-bit where quality holds.

4) GPU preference:
- Prefer H100 if available (training/optimized kernels matter), but A100-80GB is acceptable if H100 capacity is limited.

Notes: Data must remain in our VPC; we need Private control plane or Dedicated in our VPC (not shared). Also interested in high-availability across two AZs.

Let us know if you need per-endpoint latency percentiles (we can extract). Rafael, can you advise on whether 4x H100 would be a reasonable starting point given the above?

Best,
Emma
Director, ML Infrastructure
FintechCo
emma.jones@fintechco.com

Attachment: fintechco_capacity_input_v1.xlsx

Emma,

Appreciate the detailed inputs — very helpful. Rafael (SE) and Aditya (Sales Engineer) are looped in to run the sizing and validate HA/placement in your VPC. Preliminary thoughts from a quick read of the token/concurrency profile:

- GPU family: H100 preferred for the 70B model (better memory and kernel perf). If H100 constrained, we can propose an A100-80GB cluster with different sharding/quantization tradeoffs.
- Baseline cluster (very conservative starting point): 4x H100 with a dedicated KV cache layer for prefix caching to cut p95 for repeated prompts. That should handle sustained ~120 TPS and absorb short peaks to ~450 TPS with autoscaling/burst (assuming batching and 8-bit quantization where feasible).
- Alternative A100 baseline: 8x A100-80GB (80GB mem per GPU) with NVLink; will likely require more nodes but is cost-effective if H100 unavailable.
- Concurrency & batching: We'll size for 200 concurrent requests (you mentioned ~200 during peaks). We'll propose config with dynamic batching and per-route SLOs — solution will include suggested batching windows to balance latency vs cost.

Next steps (concrete):
1) Rafael — can you produce a preliminary capacity worksheet (nodes / GPU count / estimated sustained/peak RPS per node / token throughput / cost delta for H100 vs A100) against Emma's inputs?
2) Aditya — can you validate network/VPC placement and HA options (cross-AZ load balancing and private control plane)?
3) Marissa (me) — schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive next week to review Rafael's calc and confirm rollout plan.

Emma — what windows next week work for 60 minutes? We can aim for Wed/Thu morning PST.

Thanks all,
